population_scope: all 2023-24 terminal PAs whose completing pitcher has a >=9-PA pitcher_games entry
key_findings: Every multi-pitcher PA has exactly one anomalous row: pitch_number=1 pitched by a DIFFERENT real pitcher; all remaining rows match the terminal pitcher.
All anomalous first pitches are real pitches (ball/foul/swinging_strike/blocked_ball); zero automatic or pitch-clock event rows.
The anomalous pitcher pitched multiple PAs in the same game in the majority of cases (median several PAs) - genuine mid-PA pitching changes, not ID corruption and not carry-over artifacts.
51/122 have the completing pitcher in E1/E2 (0.048% of 2024 rows); 44 of the 122 are strikeouts.

Official rule (MLB Glossary; OBR Ch.9 scorer convention; cf. OBR 6.09(b) for uncaught third strike): the strikeout is credited to the pitcher who delivered the third-strike pitch, and the plate appearance is charged to the completing pitcher. The PA table's terminal-row attribution therefore MATCHES official bookkeeping for all 122 rows, including all 44 K labels.
Modeling impurity: the batter faced two pitchers within one PA. Prevalence 0.058% (2023-24).

STARTER_LEFT_RELIEVER_COMPLETED.reason: label attribution correct (completing pitcher); retained in PA-1A with split_pa flag at 0.058% prevalence; excluded from PA-1B primary start-level purity, retained in labeled sensitivity; preserved for future hook/removal research

SUSPENDED_OR_RESUMED_GAME.note: none detected; some games show two >=9-PA pitchers, consistent with resumed games, but no row required this class

canonical_future_rule: PA attributed to the COMPLETING pitcher (terminal Statcast pitch row), which equals official scorer credit; add split_pa_flag column; split PAs excluded from PA-1B primary (start-level purity) and from any pitcher-prior fitting that assumes a single-pitcher PA; retained everywhere else with disclosure.
sensitivity_rule: re-run PA-1A primary with the 51 E1/E2 split rows excluded; expected difference immaterial at 0.048% prevalence (to be measured if ever authorized).
